title: AI ROI Measurement Tools for Engineering Teams
summary: Compare AI ROI tools by cost source, output measure, and benchmark scope. See how Weave calculates cost per output hour and what that ratio cannot prove.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- **Weave's Index reports AI cost per output hour:** attributed AI spend divided by estimated expert hours of merged output for engineers with both signals in the same month. This is a cost-efficiency ratio, not financial ROI, time saved, or proof that AI caused the output.
- **An expert hour is a model estimate of the effort to complete a pull request.** It is not an engineer's recorded time, an hour saved, or the business value of the change.
- **Cost and AI attribution vary by integration.** Weave labels direct tool telemetry, commit metadata, and activity-based estimates; not every prompt, cost, or merged change can be matched to an individual.
- DX, Jellyfish, Waydev, Swarmia, and LinearB publish different cost and output measures. Compare their units only after checking the source, denominator, filters, and coverage described below.


## What should an AI ROI platform measure?


An AI coding bill tells you what you spent. An engineering intelligence platform can show what measured output coincided with that spending. It cannot turn correlation into a causal return by itself.


Weave joins AI usage and cost with the code, reviews, and delivery data behind the result. That lets engineering leaders compare tools, find productive workflows, identify wasted licenses, and explain changes in output to finance and leadership.


A useful measurement framework has four connected layers:


1. **Delivery:** deployment frequency, lead time, recovery, and reliability.
2. **Adoption:** which engineers and agents use which tools, and how that changes over time.
3. **Cost:** provider billing, token usage, subscriptions, and spend by person and tool.
4. **Output and quality:** the complexity of shipped work, review quality, reverts, and code turnover.


Keep the cost-efficiency ratio separate from financial ROI. Weave's public Index calculates **cost per output hour = total attributed AI spend ÷ estimated expert hours of merged output** for the same matched group and month. It includes only engineers with both attributed spend and merged output; ignored pull requests and unattributed organization-level overages are excluded. The cohort is Weave customer telemetry and changes over time, not a randomized industry sample. See the[AI ROI methodology](https://weaveos.com/methodology/ai-roi) for the full definition and exclusions.


**Hypothetical example, not a customer result:** $1,200 of attributed AI spend divided by 300 estimated expert hours of merged output is $4 per estimated expert hour. The inverse is 0.25 estimated expert hours per attributed dollar. Neither number shows hours saved, incremental revenue, or that AI caused the output. A financial ROI percentage needs a separately defined incremental benefit and cost: **(estimated incremental benefit − total incremental cost) ÷ total incremental cost** .


## How Weave measures cost against code output


### Measure the work, not just the number of PRs


[Silk 1](https://weaveos.com/products/code-intelligence) reads the full diff and reasons about intent, risk, and dependencies across files. Its output score represents the effort an expert engineer would need to complete that change. A three-line configuration change with consequences across forty files can receive credit for that complexity.


Every score includes a plain-language explanation. Teams can correct scores, and organization-aware calibration learns from those overrides. Use estimated expert hours as one output measure alongside PR volume, quality, and delivery. The estimate does not make different work or teams perfectly comparable, and it is not a record of time saved. Weave's public methodology explains the unit; the linked product page does not publish the sample, evaluation window, or scoring protocol behind its model-accuracy figures, so this guide does not use those figures as comparative evidence.


### Connect AI spend to engineers, tools, and output


[Token Intelligence](https://weaveos.com/products/token-intelligence) brings adoption, usage, cost, and AI-assisted output together. Weave's[AI cost coverage](https://weaveos.com/products/token-intelligence#roi) describes per-engineer cost support for supported tools. Cost-source labels distinguish vendor-billed amounts from estimates, modeled or client-reported amounts, and allocated seat costs. Coverage and attribution detail depend on the integration; some spend is available only at organization level.


Keep provider-billed spend, token-price estimates, and allocated subscriptions distinct. Reconcile cost fields against the relevant invoice or contract terms; a token-price estimate is not necessarily the amount paid. Check whether subscription-included usage is already represented before adding metered estimates, so the same expense is not counted twice. Compare the same cost basis over time.


The[AI ROI report](https://weaveos.com/products/token-intelligence#roi) brings spend and AI-attributable output together with person and tool breakdowns. Teams can use their engineering team cost or salary data in a separate financial analysis. Estimated expert hours do not become realized dollars or savings just by assigning them a salary rate.


### Keep quality and delivery in the same decision


[Engineering Intelligence](https://weaveos.com/products/engineering-intelligence) adds review depth, review cycles, reverts, code churn, incident-to-PR links, and deployment metrics. Its product page describes benchmarks using engineering data from thousands of organizations, including output per engineer, review quality, turnaround, and delivery performance. Those peer benchmarks are separate from the Weave Index's monthly matched cohort for AI cost and output. Do not treat the two populations or denominators as interchangeable.


Weave also supports[R&D capitalization](https://weaveos.com/products/token-intelligence#finops) and[portfolio reporting](https://weaveos.com/portfolio) , so the same engineering data can answer both productivity and investment questions.[Wooly](https://weaveos.com/products/wooly) lets leaders ask questions about that data in plain language.

## AI ROI tools compared


Weave publishes this guide. Product descriptions draw on the first-party pages linked below, reviewed October 17, 2026. This is a source-based comparison, not a matched hands-on benchmark. Vendor pages use different cost sources, output units, and levels of methodological detail. Where a cited page does not disclose a formula or scope, this guide marks that gap for the buyer to verify; it does not treat an undisclosed detail as proof that a product lacks the capability.


### Weave: code-based output, AI cost, and engineering intelligence


[Weave](https://weaveos.com/products/engineering-intelligence#ai-impact) connects estimated code output with supported AI usage and cost signals,[review and quality measures](https://weaveos.com/products/engineering-intelligence#reviews) ,[delivery data](https://weaveos.com/products/engineering-intelligence#benchmarks) , and financial reporting. Its public AI ROI method uses estimated expert hours of merged output and attributed AI spend for a matched cohort in the same month. The output estimate is not time saved or realized value, and the cost ratio alone does not establish causation.


The output denominator is an estimate of engineering effort, not a count of merged changes. Inspect the code and score explanation before using it to compare work. A cost-per-PR measure and a cost-per-estimated-expert-hour measure answer different questions and should not be ranked as if they shared a denominator.


### DX: developer experience and AI cost reporting


DX combines developer experience research, productivity frameworks, and AI measurement. Its[AI cost management report](https://docs.getdx.com/reports/ai-cost-management/) reports estimated spend, tokens or credits, and contributor breakdowns. The report defines estimated cost per PR as total estimated cost divided by merged PRs. DX says that merged PR and cost-per-PR metrics are unavailable when the report is filtered to a subset of AI tools; the report also requires Data Cloud and a supported AI data source.


That per-PR denominator is not complexity-adjusted output. Confirm which tools and contributors are included in the report before using it to make a vendor-level cost comparison.


### Jellyfish: investment allocation and AI token spending


[Jellyfish AI Impact](https://jellyfish.co/platform/jellyfish-ai-impact/) describes connecting AI use and spend with throughput, quality, and delivery outcomes. Its[token spend dashboard](https://jellyfish.co/platform/jellyfish-ai-impact/ai-token-usage-monitoring/) describes comparing token spend with PR throughput and forecasting costs. The cited pages do not define a shared cost-per-output formula or its cohort, so confirm those details before comparing its output with another platform's ratio.


Weave covers engineering investment questions too, including R&D capitalization, while adding Silk 1's code-based output measurement, explanations, and team calibration.


### Waydev: AI adoption and vendor unit economics


Waydev's[AI adoption page](https://waydev.co/features/ai-adoption/) advertises vendor comparisons by cost per commit, PR, and feature, with spend by developer, team, and tool. Its[AI ROI page](https://waydev.co/features/ai-roi/) describes license costs against engineering output. The cited pages do not define the calculation for each unit or explain cost-source fidelity and cohort rules. Ask how each denominator, allocation, and tool attribution is calculated before comparing results.


Cost per commit, PR, and feature use different denominators. Inspect the work behind each item and ask how cost, feature boundaries, rework, and attribution are handled before interpreting those figures as comparable ROI.


### Swarmia: team-level AI and labor costs


[Swarmia's AI ROI view](https://www.swarmia.com/changelog/2026-08-07-ai-roi/) reports monthly developer and AI costs alongside stories and epics, merged PRs, and lines changed. Its documentation defines AI cost as the list price of consumed tokens and developer cost as an administrator-configured average. These per-unit views use volume measures, not Weave's estimated expert-hour unit.


Weave adds code-level output analysis and per-engineer cost detail for supported connections, including actual provider billing where available. Use a consistent cost basis when comparing the two.


### LinearB: AI impact and workflow automation


LinearB's[platform page](https://linearb.io/platform/overview) lists AI code commits, AI review impact, and tool usage by repository alongside workflow automation. That page does not specify an AI cost source or cost-per-output formula, so confirm the relevant report's cost basis and denominator before comparing it with a cost-efficiency ratio.


Weave measures review quality and bottlenecks alongside output and spending. Teams can also use[Weave Checks](https://weaveos.com/checks) for automated pull request checks, connecting measurement with action.

Start with one decision: which AI tools to expand, which workflows to improve, or how to explain engineering investment.


Use Weave's[AI impact measurement framework](https://weaveos.com/blog/ai-impact-measurement-framework-engineering-teams) to set baselines and connect adoption signals with delivery, quality, and cost outcomes. A cost-per-output trend alone does not show that AI caused the change.


Before comparing tools, define the team, repositories, and reporting period; reconcile billed spend, subscriptions, estimates, and unallocated costs; and check whether AI attribution is direct, inferred, or estimated. Then inspect representative bug fixes, refactors, and features alongside output scores, review cycles, reverts, and delivery. Keep the metric definitions constant across the periods or tools being compared.


For delivery improvement, use Weave's review and deployment metrics. For investment allocation, use portfolio reporting and R&D capitalization. For AI budget decisions, use person and tool cost breakdowns alongside output. For a financial ROI percentage, define incremental benefits and total incremental costs with Finance; do not convert estimated expert hours into saved payroll or revenue without evidence that the capacity was actually released, avoided, or redirected to valued work.

## FAQs


### Is cost per output hour the same as financial AI ROI?


No. Cost per output hour divides attributed AI spend by estimated expert hours of merged output for a matched group and period. It does not measure saved time, incremental revenue, or causation. Financial ROI needs a separate benefit estimate, baseline, and full incremental cost calculation.


### Are DORA metrics enough to measure AI impact?


DORA tracks delivery speed and stability. AI ROI also needs adoption, spending, output, and quality. Weave connects those layers so you can see what changed and investigate why.


### Why use estimated expert hours as well as PR counts?


PRs vary in scope. Silk 1 estimates the expert effort represented by the code change and provides an explanation. That adds a complexity-aware unit alongside PR volume; it is still an estimate, not recorded time, saved hours, or business value.


### Can Weave attribute every AI prompt and cost to a person?


No. Attribution depends on the connected tool and evidence available. Weave distinguishes native integration telemetry, Git co-authorship, and activity-based estimates. Some costs are only available at organization level, and not every prompt or bill can be matched to a specific engineer and merged change. Check the[methodology and cost coverage](https://weaveos.com/methodology/ai-roi) for the integration you use.


### Does Weave report costs per engineer?


For supported integrations, yes. Per-engineer coverage and cost source vary by tool. Weave labels provider billing, estimates, modeled or client-reported amounts, and allocated subscription costs. See[cost coverage](https://weaveos.com/products/token-intelligence#roi) before comparing vendors or teams.


### Does Weave support finance and engineering investment reporting?


Yes. Weave includes R&D capitalization, portfolio reporting, and AI spend analysis alongside engineering output, quality, reviews, and delivery benchmarks.


### Should subscription fees and token usage both be included?


Include the costs your organization actually pays. Keep subscriptions, included allowances, and usage charges distinguishable to avoid double counting. Weave's cost-source labels and Financial settings help you use the appropriate basis. Keep estimates separate from billed amounts and document any allocation rule for shared costs.
